title: Coinbase Q3 collateral disclosure, Circle payment-rail expansion, and XRP-specific evidence limits

append_only.purpose: Add balance-sheet collateral detail, unnamed counterparty concentration, Circle payment-network expansion, and competing XRP substitution/complementarity hypotheses.

source_capture_policy.reason: Primary SEC and issuer pages were reviewed through rendered web extracts; no byte-complete source payloads or independent transport receipts were captured.

claims_supported: Q3 2026 total revenue was $1.215582B; Q3 2026 stablecoin revenue was $306.905M versus $324.534M in Q3 2025.
Coinbase says its Circle arrangement was renewed on the same terms and the 2026 presentation reclassification did not change the arrangement or revenue generated.
One counterparty accounted for 27% of total revenue in Q3 2026; the filing passage does not name that counterparty.
At September 30, 2026, recognized lending collateral totaled $1.009297B: $11.740M fiat/payment stablecoins and $997.557M crypto assets.
Recognized crypto lending collateral comprised $920.649M Bitcoin, $67.005M Ethereum and $9.903M aggregate other crypto assets.
Additional borrower collateral not recognized as an asset/liability totaled $3.284562B: $480.450M fiat/payment stablecoins and $2.804112B crypto assets.
Recognized derivatives collateral totaled $325.766M and the table identifies Bitcoin and Ethereum; collateral requirements were at least 100% of derivative notional.
Fiat/payment-stablecoin loan receivables were $1.958539B versus crypto-asset loan receivables of $17.598M.
limitations: The filing contains no XRP-specific collateral, custody, loan, derivative or trading-volume figure; a text search for XRP returned no match.
The $2.804112B unrecognized borrower crypto-collateral balance is not broken down by asset, so XRP exposure cannot be ruled in or out.
The $9.903M other-crypto recognized lending-collateral line is aggregate and does not identify constituent assets.
The unnamed 27% revenue counterparty must not be attributed to Circle without separate evidence.
The 10-Q's issuer disclosures are not independent market telemetry.

claims_supported: Q3 2026 average USDC circulation was $73.3B, up 8% year over year; quarter-end circulation was $73.9B, flat year over year.
Q3 2026 USDC on-chain transaction volume was $13.9T, up 49% year over year.
Total revenue and reserve income was $864.888M; reserve income was $657.624M versus $711.241M a year earlier; other revenue was $207.264M versus $28.518M.
Circle's earnings materials identify approximately $182M of ARC token presale revenue within other revenue.
Circle Payments Network reported $41.3B annualized TPV; this is an annualized company metric, not realized quarterly TPV.

Circle announced a definitive agreement to acquire Tazapay, expected to close in 2027 subject to regulatory approvals; Tazapay's own reported annualized payment volume exceeds $25B and about 60% of its transaction volume already includes stablecoins.
Circle says Arc public mainnet launched September 16, 2026 with more than 100 institutional and ecosystem builders and native USDC integration.
Circle announced Visa Direct stablecoin prefunding had moved from pilots to commercial deployment through Inyo Global, with USDC payouts across 180+ countries.
Circle announced eligible U.S. Samsung Wallet users can send USDC to qualifying bank accounts in more than 60 countries.
Circle's Q3 materials describe Binance's $100M equity investment and a renewed five-year USDC distribution partnership.
limitations: USDC on-chain transaction volume is gross ledger activity, not unique payments, net capital inflow, or XRP demand.
Gross minting/redemption figures are not net supply changes.
The ARC presale materially affects other revenue; total Circle growth must not be attributed solely to USDC reserve economics.
Tazapay acquisition and its payment volume are not yet Circle-owned/closed operations; closing is expected in 2027 subject to approvals.
Visa Direct, Samsung Wallet and Arc disclosures do not establish XRP or XRPL usage.

claims_supported: Average USDC held in Coinbase products reached $22B, up 49% year over year, according to Coinbase's earnings release.
Coinbase described this product-held balance as approximately 30% of average USDC market capitalization.
limitations: The $22B average balance is sourced to the earnings release, not the retrieved 10-Q passage.
Average product-held USDC is a stock measure, not net new USDC issuance or proof of XRP demand.

claims_supported: Fuelmaps displayed XRP mid $1.3238 across six venues at its 09:00 UTC hourly snapshot.
Displayed bids/asks were $8.4M/$5.7M within 0.5%, $11.2M/$8.1M within 1%, $13.1M/$10.8M within 2%, $18.2M/$16.4M within 5%, and $22.3M/$20.2M within 10%.
Displayed bid share ranged from 52.5% to 59.5% across the reported bands.
limitations: One aggregator publisher; six venues are not six independent publishers.
Binance and Bitget are excluded; OKX and Kraken contribute near-price depth only, while full-depth coverage comes from Coinbase, Bitstamp, Bitfinex and Gemini.
Displayed orders may be cancelled and hidden/iceberg liquidity is not visible.
Hourly columns average one-minute snapshots and are not a single instantaneous executable book.

claims_supported: Displayed aggregate XRP perpetual open interest of $884.00M across its stated seven-contract coverage, +0.0100% weighted funding per eight hours and $1.62B 24-hour volume.
Displayed Binance XRPUSDT open interest of $448.68M.
limitations: Publisher coverage and contract inclusion require raw exchange-level reconciliation.
Dashboard value is not an independently receipted exchange response.

claims_supported: Displayed Binance XRPUSDT open interest of $450.4M, +0.0100% funding per period, 72% of accounts long and 69% of top-trader position size long.
The dashboard reported 24-hour OI down 0.3% while price rose 2.9%; its seven-day view reported OI +13% in XRP units while price was 1.2% lower.
limitations: Account counts and top-trader positioning are not total notional exposure.
Exchange liquidation feeds are incomplete and dashboard figures are not raw receipts.

claims_supported: Displayed seven-exchange XRP perpetual open interest of $2.08B, +3.70% over 24 hours, +0.0100% OI-weighted funding per eight hours and at least $5.19M in 24-hour liquidations.
Displayed 76.3% long accounts and exchange-specific Binance OI of $542.62M.
limitations: Publisher reports a 15-minute delay and incomplete liquidation reporting.
Its Binance OI differs materially from the other two dashboards and is not reconciled to the same contract universe or exact timestamp.

coinbase_q3_2026_usd_millions.derivatives_collateral_requirement: At least 100% of derivative notional value.

collateral_reconciliation.xrp_specific_conclusion: The 10-Q does not name XRP. The $2.804112B unrecognized customer crypto-collateral balance is not asset-broken-down, so XRP exposure remains unknown; no XRP-specific amount can be asserted. The recognized derivative-collateral table identifies BTC and ETH only.

revenue_concentration.attribution_rule: Do not infer that the unnamed 27% revenue counterparty is Circle. Coinbase separately confirms its Circle arrangement and investment, but the concentration note does not name the counterparty.

spot_book_snapshot.interpretation: Displayed bid depth exceeded asks in the sampled bands; this is a descriptive one-hour aggregate, not durable support or a forecast.

derivatives_disagreement.conclusion: The Kodexius and Seandra Binance readings are close despite different dashboard designs; TradRadar's Binance value is materially higher. Aggregate OI differs by more than 2x. Do not average or label this as a verified market-wide OI increase without synchronized raw contract-level snapshots and a reconciled exchange/contract universe.

competing_hypotheses.statement: Circle's Arc network, Visa Direct USDC prefunding, Samsung Wallet, Binance distribution and Tazapay expansion may substitute for some XRP bridge/settlement use cases.
supporting_evidence: Visa Direct USDC prefunding moved to commercial deployment
Tazapay acquisition announced with stablecoin-heavy transaction volume
disconfirming_evidence_required: Evidence that the rails use XRP as an intermediary
Cross-chain transactions showing XRP liquidity legs
Issuer or payment-provider disclosure of XRPL routing

competing_hypotheses.statement: Circle's multi-chain distribution may expand stablecoin use overall and could complement XRPL where users choose RLUSD/USDC on XRPL or use XRP for a separate bridge leg.
supporting_evidence: RLUSD is distributed on XRPL by Coinbase
disconfirming_evidence_required: Sustained migration of relevant payment volume away from XRPL
No measurable XRP bridge or DEX liquidity demand despite stablecoin growth

competing_hypotheses.statement: Coinbase's large unrecognized borrower crypto-collateral balance could contain XRP, but the 10-Q does not disclose the asset composition.
disconfirming_evidence_required: Asset-level collateral schedules showing no XRP
Counterparty or product disclosures identifying the entire balance

competing_hypotheses.statement: The 27% single-counterparty revenue concentration may be economically material, but the filing does not identify the counterparty.
disconfirming_evidence_required: A primary filing or explicit issuer statement naming the counterparty

competing_hypotheses.statement: Positive funding and high account-long ratios suggest a long-leaning sample, but aggregate open interest and venue coverage disagree materially.
disconfirming_evidence_required: Raw synchronized exchange position, OI and funding data
Venue-by-venue contract reconciliation and verified liquidation streams

reasons: No byte-complete source captures or SHA-256 receipts for rendered web pages.
No independent timestamp anchoring for the dashboard observations.
Coinbase's customer collateral balance is not asset-broken-down.
Derivative dashboards do not reconcile to a common contract universe.
Issuer-reported volume and annualized TPV are not equivalent to net capital flows or XRP settlement volume.
